# Bulkhead spec

Spec version: 0.1.0

Conflict order: security, then performance, then flexibility (SPEC-3).

A green report means no known leak paths, not proof of none.

| TENANT-1 | invariant | proposed | Tenant identity is derived only from the hostname or the session, never from a body, header or query parameter. | A client-supplied tenant ID lets any caller name another tenant. | Structural: the tenant resolver accepts only host and session inputs. Verified by canary scenario. | canary | `tenant-isolation/identity-from-host-or-session-only` |
| TENANT-2 | invariant | proposed | The only database handle a route handler receives is scoped to the resolved tenant and offers no way to name another tenant. | A query bug must not be able to reach another tenant's rows. | Structural: handlers get a scoped handle; raw bindings are not exported. | canary | `tenant-isolation/scoped-handle-only` |
| TENANT-3 | contract | proposed | Each tenant's data lives in its own Durable Object SQLite database; only tenants, domains and billing state live in the shared control plane. | Physical separation makes cross-tenant reads unrepresentable rather than merely filtered. | Structural: per-tenant Durable Object storage; control-plane schema allow-list. | canary | `tenant-isolation/per-tenant-database` |
| TENANT-4 | invariant | proposed | Adding a tenant never changes any response another tenant receives. | Shared caches, keys or namespaces would leak or couple tenants. | Verify metamorphic scenario: compare tenant A responses before and after tenant B is added. | metamorphic | `tenant-isolation/adding-tenant-is-invisible` |
| TENANT-5 | invariant | proposed | A marker planted in tenant A never appears in any response, log, cache entry or export visible to tenant B. | Logs, caches and derived copies are alternate readers that bypass table-level isolation. | Verify canary scenario across responses, logs and exports. | canary | `tenant-isolation/canary-does-not-cross` |
